description: The figure presents three pie charts showing the distribution of problems by correctness category under chain-of-thought (CoT), separated by difficulty level (easy, medium, hard), with four slices per chart corresponding to the legend categories N+K+ (teal), N−K+ (yellow), N−K− (orange), and N+K− (red). In the easy chart, the slices are labeled approximately 40.6% (teal, N+K+), 45.9% (yellow, N−K+), 10.1% (orange, N−K−), and 3.3% (red, N+K−), with percentage labels printed inside the slices. In the medium chart, the slices are approximately 44.6% (teal, N+K+), 44.3% (yellow, N−K+), 7.2% (orange, N−K−), and 3.9% (red, N+K−), again with internal percentage labels. In the hard chart, the slices are approximately 20.1% (teal, N+K+), 36.2% (yellow, N−K+), 36.8% (orange, N−K−), and 7.0% (red, N+K−), with the same internal labeling. A legend appears to the right mapping colors to the four categories, no slices are exploded or otherwise emphasized, and the slice ordering varies by chart rather than following a consistent descending-size arrangement.
caption_used: Problem distribution based on correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using CoT. The results indicate that while easier problems are primarily hindered by a lack of knowledge (N−K+ at approximately 50%), medium problems show a consistent dominance of reasoning-based errors (N−K− at 15%). For hard problems, the primary bottleneck lies in the inability to integrate geometric reasoning, as evidenced by the sharp decline in N+K+ to below 10%.
